witnesses.provenance: Solana's per-transaction MAX_COMPUTE_UNIT_LIMIT is 1,400,000 compute units; the chain's limit, not ours. The observed maximum is 488,773 on the initializer -- 35% of the ceiling for ONE pre-Market bootstrap, and the largest single figure this row measured anywhere.
A `wire_bytes` of null says the campaign did not measure, which is honest but is not a claim that the frame fits. This campaign measured nothing before 2026-09-01.

The same instruction was 1,797 bytes as a legacy message -- 565 over Solana's 1,232-byte PACKET_DATA_BYTES -- so this route had never been submittable anywhere; ProgramTest submits no packet, which is exactly why it survived. It now executes as a v0 message over a frozen Address Lookup Table whose 41 addresses are derived from the instruction's own account metas, leaving only the transaction payer and the invoked caller program inline. 41 x 31 bytes saved, less the 36 the lookup entry costs, is the 1,235 between the two figures. Nothing about the instruction moved: same data, same 43 metas, same privileges, same program, and no ABI, Lean artifact or refusal code changed. The two hostiles share the frame and measure 561, one address lower because each aliases a coordinate onto another already in the set.

Against the same 1,232-byte PACKET_DATA_BYTES. The abort side of the pair is 1,002 bytes and fits with 230 to spare, which is the asymmetry worth writing down: unwinding a pre-Market funding is submittable by anyone on a plain legacy message, while creating one is not.

witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select(.error != null) | [.logs[] | select(test("failed: custom program error"))] | first | capture("0x(?<c>[0-9a-f]+)").c] | unique | sort | join(",")
witnesses.provenance: Read off the FIRST `failed:` line of each refusal, which is the frame that originated the code -- a propagated refusal is re-reported by every frame it unwinds through. 0x3001 is core/CoreSbfError::AccountFrame, 0x8000 is resolution/ResolutionError::AccountFrame and 0x800e is resolution/ResolutionError::Funding, in the registered bands 3 and 8 (crates/dclutch-refusal-registry). Two programs, three codes. All three of these hostiles asserted only is_err() before this tier existed, and the two AccountFrame refusals were indistinguishable under that assertion despite coming from different programs at different CPI depths.

Against Solana's 1,232-byte PACKET_DATA_BYTES. The previous witness pinned one route's figure; this one is the campaign-wide claim, and it is the one that would catch a new row added over the limit rather than an existing row changing. It excludes nulls on purpose: an unmeasured transaction is not a transaction that fits, and `pre-market-measured-every-transaction` is what holds that count at zero.
